summary: Keep expanded test source open and current during file edits. Add focused reader checks for matching-result precedence, refreshed and broken test links, late source responses after navigation, and the syntax coloring size boundary. Update description and catalog links without adding a test framework.

examined.reason: Only expanded-test state during content refresh changes. Paragraph and summary comparisons, toggle persistence, and comparison bases are unchanged.
Passage resolution and direct or multi-destination navigation are unchanged; existing smoke assertions remain intact.

The refresh implementation now preserves expanded tests on content changes; its exact source selector is refreshed. Identity changes still clear detail state and project changes still clear expansions. The background refresh and hierarchy navigation account remains accurate.
Parent-child selection, independent scroll and source ownership are unchanged. The retained state concerns only test rows within the same selection.
No title-bar, project-selection, summary, keyboard, or View controls change. Project changes still clear expanded tests.

Describes and links retained expansions and fresh source on edits, broken-link display, and isolation of detached rows. New checks cover content refresh, missing passages, delayed success/failure and current-result precedence.

The existing coloring limit, exact text and passage behavior are correct; new assertions exercise exactly 200000 and 200001 characters, same-path cache changes, and retained implementation beside refreshed tests.
Production markup construction, IPC and content isolation do not change. The browser test helper imports production renderers only inside the test process.
Markdown, equations and image rendering are untouched; their assertion group remains part of the complete desktop check.
Description relations, implementation link shapes, statuses and dependency meaning are unchanged.
The broader promise of background-refreshed descriptions and contextual test evidence is preserved and made more consistent; no new view or authority is introduced.
Summary storage, validity and per-description responsibility do not change; existing summary checks remain intact.
No result schema, recording, exact-tree matching or acceptance behavior changes. Synthetic fixture records are explicitly labeled and test the existing reader precedence rule.
Tree layout, folding, revision selection and selection return are unchanged; their existing smoke assertions remain intact.

Navigation still relies on the same stable identities, working or historical project reads, and exact passage matches. Retaining an expanded test during refresh changes no hierarchy or link semantics.

results.method: npm run typecheck; npm run test:desktop; node src/cli.ts validate
results.environment: macOS, Node v24.16.0, Electron 43.2.0 with Playwright; isolated temporary queue projects
results.evidence: TypeScript check and full Electron smoke both exited 0; validation found no issues. All 11 cataloged desktop assertion groups completed, including current-result precedence over newer stale evidence, retained expanded code after edits, missing-passage error and repair, delayed success and failure after pane replacement, and exact 200000/200001-character highlighting boundary with cache transitions. Before the fix, the expanded-row regression failed with null open state. Logs: /private/tmp/stratic-reader-typecheck.txt and /private/tmp/stratic-reader-desktop.txt. The unit suite was not rerun for this renderer-only production change.

unmapped.reason: Shared imports and the small assertion helper support the two directly linked browser checks. They are test scaffolding, not a separate product responsibility.
